cards.title: Document scope
items: This document includes issue #14 memory-profile comparison and issue #13 public host/runtime matrix evidence from October 24, 2026. The comparison froze two synthetic tasks and two exact profiles before twelve public processor calls. Eleven calls committed memory and one Pi project-memory call failed. Summary calls covered only the first assistant completion, leaving later tool/user events pending. Semantic assessment and limits are separate from structural success. Sources: docs/MEMORY_PROFILE_COMPARISON.md, docs/evidence/memory-profile-comparison-2026-10-24/freeze.json, docs/evidence/memory-profile-comparison-2026-10-24/runtime-analysis.json.

A separate local Git snapshot pins the source files. Its revision is separate from the main repository history. source-manifest.json records the base HEAD, file list, and hashes. source-snapshot.bundle preserves the snapshot for later checks.
The diagram, supporting text, Archify controls, and HTML language attribute use English.

This refresh also describes mandatory material support, isolated original-report interpretation, bound summary outcome checks and the trusted Pi native schema helper. Historical comparison and development outcomes remain historical; this architecture is a source-backed description, not private semantic acceptance or installation proof. Sources: docs/adr/0012-review-session-summary-support.md:92-110,116-132.

cards.title: Material support and summary outcomes
items: After output shape validation, summary-support-v5 reviews every complete nonempty material field in retained notes and summaries against role-labelled current/history evidence. Note title, body, tags and structured observation fields retain typed arrays and record ownership. Observation classifications follow the same scoped evidence rules as prose. Code supplies exact field spans and original-report anchors; one to eight comparison rows per unit and at most 64 rows must cover all units. Outcome-field comparisons bind report_text, reported_content, other or unresolved. Request, next_steps and note units use outside_outcome. Binding proves text ownership, not semantic truth. Sources: codex_mem/summary_support.py:99-147,165-256,309-385; codex_mem/observation_contract.py:3-15; codex_mem/processor.py:489-529. The output schema now exposes the existing per-owner row branches: note/request/next_steps units require outside_outcome with empty candidate/report bindings, while each outcome unit selects only its own candidate spans and permitted report-binding branches. The unchanged local validator remains authoritative. Schema shape and owned references do not prove semantic support. Sources: codex_mem/summary_support.py:254-297,309-385.

After original support passes for a summary, summary-source-v4 sees only the latest current original assistant report between code-selected delimiters absent from that body. Provenance and current order stay in code-owned validation context. No candidate, competing request, history or historical fallback reaches this interpretation. Up to eight content propositions plus language and organization slots preserve target, subject, time, modality and scope. The outcome-v5 layer joins the exact selected original body by retained identity, provenance, SHA-256 and complete ordered span coverage before dispatch. It pairs each immutable bound summary claim with the selected source items, at most fifty relations; request, next_steps and note fields remain outside this layer. Full report text remains visible because extraction is incomplete. Missing or changed joins fail before dispatch. Sources: codex_mem/summary_outcome.py:49-107,122-173,189-312.

Every call uses the same selected profile and shared deadline. One correction allowance is shared by structural repair, mandatory support and optional Jev review. Changed note or summary records repeat mandatory support with fresh retained evidence; applicable summary reviews also repeat. Exact unchanged rejected record/evidence/interpretation/profile/versions retain that record's first rejection with no new vote. This can preserve a mistaken rejection. Lease/source checks precede reuse. Store captures per-record identities with the exact current/history views before excerpting. The processor compares those identities before Jev filtering, cache reuse, live chunk submission after HTTP-slot acquisition, and selection. Native initial/correction turns, support/source/outcome calls and optional quality use the same checks before submission. The original absolute deadlines remain. A guard denies changes visible then; it cannot revoke a submitted request or close the interval after a guard. The atomic write fence still blocks stale output. No lock spans a model call. Full retained fields, metadata, source links and hydrated current tool I/O remain bound. Store rechecks the same IDs and content fingerprint inside the output write transaction, before inserting any note or summary. The cross-session project_context is reference-only for generation and optional quality; it retains existence checks and is excluded from mandatory support evidence and this content fingerprint. Deleted or changed evidence blocks the whole packet; unrelated records do not. No model call runs in this transaction. Known semantic failures quarantine only their batch while fresh work continues; operational failures retain project blocking. Sources: codex_mem/processor.py, codex_mem/service.py, tests/test_summary_support.py, codex_mem/store.py, tests/test_summary_outcome.py. A replaced lease preserves summary_support_stale without changing its replacement. Sources: codex_mem/processor.py:469-473,489-520; docs/adr/0012-review-session-summary-support.md:78-92.

The execution_calls ledger records generation, up to two original-support calls, one source interpretation and two outcome calls. Generation includes at most two turns, so the attempt has at most seven native model calls. All share the selected profile and original deadline; note-only packets omit the derived source/outcome layer. Independent measured counters add once; any missing counter keeps that combined counter null. Recovery and terminal receipts derive these aggregates from persisted execution_calls instead of adding prior totals. Unfinished calls remain partial; late generation receipts cannot erase reviewer gaps. Whole-attempt elapsed time counts nested reviews once. Reviewer failures retain their own metrics and identifiers and cannot replace the completed generation receipt. Diagnostics contain only fixed subtypes, status, versions and fingerprints. Stored note/summary shapes and verification labels remain unchanged. Sources: codex_mem/observer_usage_store.py:444-468,519-564,634-643; codex_mem/processor.py:376-404,447-487,489-556; docs/adr/0012-review-session-summary-support.md:96-100. For the first decoded processed candidate only, a reported missing_required_summary can request that existing correction. This reported first reason does not prove the absence of other errors. The second candidate must pass all normal shape, source, support and applicable outcome checks; no third generation or partial note write is allowed. Malformed JSON, unknown handles and other reported reasons do not gain this path. The returned generation_correction contains the exact initial reason and a parsed, source-resolved canonical candidate fingerprint. Durable generation.review_diagnostic keeps its existing five keys and records invalid/structure plus fingerprints, not the exact initial reason or raw output. Sources: codex_mem/processor.py:610-645,755-760,806-814.

Historical acceptance6 on the earlier committed source failed: five of ten required useful outputs were produced. The later owner-schema, missing-summary correction and generic wording repairs have offline authored checks only; the historical native run did not exercise these source bytes. They do not establish semantic improvement, independent truth or successful private acceptance. Model/profile settings are unchanged by these repairs. New semantic validation requires separate authorization. Sources: docs/adr/0012-review-session-summary-support.md:142-154; docs/EXECUTION.md:130-138.

Outcome decisions distinguish applicability, residual scope and value. Absent or disjoint comparisons are unused. Available same-scope compatible values are checked; incompatible values contradict. Unresolved applicable comparisons and unavailable evidence for an asserted same-scope property remain uncertain. Contradiction or uncertainty blocks storage. Compatibility does not independently establish original support. Sources: codex_mem/summary_outcome.py:315-365.

Generation and review instructions preserve only the actual observed execution scope. They do not invent local, regression, synthetic or production labels. Ambiguous candidate references can use context only from the same unit_records owner; permitted original-source and historical context remain available under existing rules. Evidence-limit wording is also checked for implied events or success. Incidental candidate-format descriptions are omitted. The candidate remains non-evidence. Semantic meaning is judged fallibly by the model; code validates shape, ownership and references. Sources: codex_mem/processor.py:2040-2061; codex_mem/summary_support.py:206-250,388-397.

cards.title: Independent Pi installation
items: The release root package declares pi/extension.ts and carries the shared Python payload. The project installer stages a managed .pi/codex-mem copy, records an absolute Python executable and shared memory directory, then merges one native MCP server and one local package declaration. Codex installation and executables are not required. Sources: package.json, scripts/install_pi.py:68-166, pi/extension.ts:16-42.

Updates retain the recorded shared memory selection when no override is supplied. Fresh and legacy resolved memory paths inside the replaceable package are rejected before mutation. Disable and uninstall retain even a legacy nested store, payload and shared service. Personal Pi settings and unrelated resources remain separate. Sources: scripts/install_pi.py:68-123,229-255, tests/test_pi_install.py, docs/PI_INSTALL.md.

Installation checks pin Pi 1.4.0, validate the recorded extension/MCP launch paths, exercise the recorded Python interpreter and report each selected background executable separately. Missing Codex does not block loading, capture or startup. Users select Pi profiles and native authorization explicitly. Separate matrix and diagnostic quality results retain their own limits in docs/HOST_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md and docs/MEMORY_PROFILE_COMPARISON.md. Sources: scripts/install_pi.py:169-226, tests/test_pi_install.py, docs/PI_INSTALL.md.

cards.title: Execution diagnostics and usage
items: CLI doctor and the dashboard read saved profiles and bounded attempt metadata without dispatching a model. Default and processor overrides remain visible beside requested and actual identity. Latest failures have fixed content-free actions. Explicit doctor --check-execution shares native preparation with the processors. Sources: codex_mem/execution_diagnostics.py, codex_mem/dashboard_data.py, docs/EXECUTION.md.

Pi checks the exact 1.4.0 version and uses auth check --json --no-refresh before RPC selection. Codex reads account/read without requesting refresh, then validates the exact catalog model and reasoning. Missing executables, native authorization, model or reasoning support have separate reasons. Codex required-protocol support does not establish universal version compatibility. Local credential readiness does not prove remote acceptance. Sources: codex_mem/processor.py:1021-1039,1690-1745, codex_mem/pi_runtime.py:184-197,368-433, docs/PI_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE.json.

Reports combine historical Codex and new observation/project-memory attempts. Runtime-qualified worker identifiers preserve collisions across runtimes. Per-counter known subtotals remain separate from unknown totals. Failed measured usage, cumulative counter replacement, and original provenance remain visible. API estimates do not establish actual charges, and Pi receives no Codex-credit estimate. Sources: codex_mem/cost_report.py, codex_mem/pricing.py, codex_mem/observer_usage_store.py, tests/test_execution_usage_reports.py. Interruption recovery replaces top-level counters, usage status and update counts from the saved independent-call ledger inside the existing transaction. It preserves the raw ledger, generation identity/provenance and known duration. Any missing counter remains null, and a running measured call prevents complete status. A terminal generation receipt cannot restore certainty missing from a reviewer. Legacy rows without a call ledger retain their prior behavior. Only the existing explicit whole-attempt measurement contract can replace duration; nested wall times are never summed. These are recovery/accounting rules, not proof of an observed live crash. Sources: codex_mem/observer_usage_store.py:149-187,215-256,519-564,634-643.

cards.title: Host/runtime evidence boundaries
items: The common matrix submits Codex hooks or the public Pi local protocol into a real temporary Store. Observation cases drain the durable service queue in a fresh process. Project-memory cases drain the durable project-memory queue through its public explicit processor in a fresh process, without bypassing the service quiet period. Only external executables are deterministic. Pi/Pi excludes Codex from PATH. Sources: tests/test_host_runtime_matrix.py:25-122, docs/HOST_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md.

All four pairs exercise roles, source references, project scope, duplicates, privacy, injected-memory exclusion, atomic protocol failure, retained-source retry, and deletion during generation. Concurrent Codex/Pi events exercise two worker slots and retain the active profile while a later attempt reloads changed configuration. Existing suites own native lifecycle, tools, legacy migration and usage coverage. Sources: tests/test_host_runtime_matrix.py:124-323, docs/HOST_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md.

Installed Pi lifecycle and MCP tests use real native Pi with a deterministic local HTTP provider. The separate live helper sends synthetic public-adapter events through real background executables and remote providers into disposable memory. All four observation pairs recorded processed derived notes with exact execution identity, source/project references, and next-request delivery. Pi/Pi excluded Codex. Pi was 1.4.0 and Codex CLI was 0.163.0. These runs do not establish native interactive event emission, hook trust, other processors or model quality. Sources: docs/evidence/host-runtime-matrix-2026-10-24/live-final.json, scripts/live_host_runtime_smoke.py, docs/HOST_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md.

The final live report identifies its adapter boundary and uncovered processors. The executed helper was reconstructed from the recorded edit sequence after the run, not captured before it. Later helper edits strengthened future classification, audit fields and safe failure diagnostics without another remote run. Failures record the stage and allowlisted cause metadata without raw exception text, process output or paths. The provenance file records both hashes and the exact prior pass predicates. Current classifier and diagnostic coverage uses routine tests. Sources: docs/evidence/host-runtime-matrix-2026-10-24/snapshot-provenance.json, scripts/live_host_runtime_smoke.py:64-92, tests/test_live_host_runtime_smoke.py.

The quality comparison observes real native execution through a recorder at the public execution boundary, with temporary stores and synthetic sources. It retains original parsed packets, durable IDs, failures, latency and usage. Generation remains single-use; up to five ordered review executions use distinct bounded paths. Timeline output bodies are previews, structured metadata is complete, and project-memory snapshots retain typed fields. Invalid raw model text is unavailable from the adapter boundary. Independent semantic grading remains distinct from core acceptance. Sources: scripts/memory_profile_comparison.py, tests/test_memory_profile_comparison.py, docs/MEMORY_PROFILE_COMPARISON.md.

The shared redactor skips replacement passes only for ASCII text without any necessary redaction marker. Every possible match and all non-ASCII text retain the existing full redactor. Redaction precedes truncation. The hook supervisor keeps its two-second worker deadline and existing failure notice. Cold-source public capture tests exclude bytecode caches. Sources: codex_mem/privacy.py, tests/test_privacy.py, tests/test_hook_large_payload.py, docs/EXECUTION.md.

cards.title: Host and background execution
items: Codex and Pi are interactive hosts. Their model selection does not select the background runtime. Both processors submit bounded generation requests through the shared contract. Each request carries a job type, schema, profile, monotonic deadline, and attempt identifier. Sources: execution.py:73-121, processor.py:647-681, episode_processor.py:908-917.

NativeProcessorRunner preserves Codex completion, exact identity, tool restrictions, and usage. PiProcessorRunner connects both processors to a pinned Pi 1.4.0 subprocess. It waits for agent_settled, a completed assistant response, and matching idle state. Prompt acceptance is not completion. Sources: execution.py:166-203, processor.py:1005-1220, pi_runtime.py:453-519.

The resolver chooses the processor override, default profile, then legacy Codex. Observations, summaries, project memory, reconsideration, and consolidation can use Pi with independent profiles. Pi catalog, exact provider/model selection, advertised thinking, and pre/post state checks share one deadline. Unsupported profiles fail without substitution. Sources: execution.py:15-70, episode_processor.py:839-840,908-917, pi_runtime.py:387-434,453-491, docs/EXECUTION.md.

Pi 1.4.0 may emit one thinking_level_changed notification while set_model applies its own level. Preparation accepts at most one exact type/level record with a known native level, then requires the selected model to advertise it. Duplicate, extra-field and unknown notifications fail. The adapter next assigns the requested level explicitly; its command accepts only that exact level. Initial and completed state checks still require the selected provider, model and requested thinking level. This bounded model-switch handling applies across providers. Sources: codex_mem/pi_runtime.py:407-433,254-272; docs/PI_RUNTIME.md:15-19.

Observation jobs keep their source identity across profile changes. The claim transaction stores each requested profile with its lease. Corrections retain it; later attempts reload current configuration. Legacy receipts preserve requested-only provenance and measured usage. Successful sources do not replay, including overlapping historical jobs. Explicit maintenance recovery retains its separate fingerprint and opt-in. Explicit retry_failed with a different processor can create distinct work; successful sources and one-shot recovery remain protected. Sources: store.py:2442-2949, observer_usage_store.py:81-147,292-311, tests/test_observation_profiles.py. Project memory retains its existing profile-independent source fingerprint and stores requested and verified execution separately. Additive migration preserves historical values; failed usage survives source deletion. Sources: project_memory.py:494-599, tests/test_project_memory_profiles.py.

The runtime proposes data and has no memory-write interface. Source roles, evidence validation, leases, and atomic writes remain with the processors and Store. Source custody and episode consolidation retain their existing rules. Sources: processor.py:686-716, episode_processor.py:925-949.

Pi creates a fresh temporary working directory, agent profile and in-memory session. Only native auth/models are linked. Tools, MCP, extension discovery, skills, instructions, automatic retries and compaction remain disabled. For openai-codex summary_support jobs only, execution explicitly loads one package-owned hash-pinned schema helper. It registers no tools, provider clients, routing, output handlers or continuations, and changes only text.format. Generation and other providers keep prompt-schema behavior. These are runtime restrictions, not an OS sandbox. Sources: codex_mem/pi_runtime.py:368-400,453-474; codex_mem/pi_schema_helper.js:7-42; codex_mem/pi_schema.py:27-60.

The additive Pi receipt separates configured CLI restrictions from observed identity, settlement, stop reason, and tool events. It does not invent Codex checks or an enumerated tool inventory. Streaming counters replace current-generation totals; corrections add each generation once. Missing usage stays unknown or partial, including Pi zero placeholders. Failed packets retain measured usage. Sources: pi_runtime.py:200-364, project_memory.py:550-593, observer_usage_store.py:313-698, execution.py:214-252. Observation Pi checkpoints retain measured totals while omitted optional counters remain null. Public capture, summary, context, recovery and mixed-profile tests: tests/test_pi_observations.py. Structured output receipts distinguish prompt_schema from strict_json_schema and carry only the allowed proof hashes, status and temporary transport/retry policy. Source: codex_mem/execution.py:231-252.

Strict Pi review uses temporary SSE transport, cache warming off and zero provider retries. Acceptance requires one exact applied proof matching helper/schema hashes, selected provider/model, strict format and unchanged remaining payload. Missing, foreign, duplicate, oversized or tampered proof rejects acceptance. Pi catches hook errors, so this fence cannot retract an already-sent request. Receipts disclose bundled_schema_only and structured-output mode, hashes and status. The bundled helper is Python package data. Sources: codex_mem/pi_schema.py:53-105; codex_mem/pi_schema_helper.js:14-40; codex_mem/pi_runtime.py:357-364,487-491; pyproject.toml:29-30.

cards.title: Shared host events and context
items: Codex adapts native hooks to HostEvent. Pi 1.4.0 observes message_end, resolves native entry IDs after persistence, and submits only current-runtime sources at agent_settled. It never imports existing history or captures streaming updates. Python applies shared privacy, project policy, source identity and queue wake. Pi tool-call IDs retain opaque pipe separators in source metadata and tool provenance. Other identifier restrictions and bounded batch validation remain unchanged. Sources: host.py:48-214, hooks.py:882-929, pi/extension.ts:107-177, pi_host.py:24-125.

Legacy Codex source names and session IDs remain valid. Other host and branch sessions have separate namespaces. One classifier serves SQL queue and retrieval filters, processor summary validation, and project memory. Old dedupe aliases preserve existing entry IDs without a migration or replay. They remove injected memory before hashing, as the old Codex adapter did. Sources: host.py:21-65, store.py:1819-2066.

ContextRequest returns bounded untrusted data with omission diagnostics. Codex owns hook framing. Pi receives custom memory at startup and before prompts; only its current custom context reaches the model, and it is excluded from capture. Empty or failed refreshes remove prior automatic memory while preserving unrelated custom messages. Tiny budgets omit the frame and report a bounded native status. The local Python protocol has byte, event, response and deadline limits. Failure does not block conversation. Sources: host.py:230-297, hooks.py:823-879, pi/extension.ts:16-67,98-140,178-191, pi_host.py:128-164.

Pi has no native private flag on UserMessage. Explicit private markers activate the shared gate for user, assistant and tool sources. Complete tool JSON is decoded before shared redaction. The shared safe payload reader checks both stored raw reads and new Pi source bodies. Incoming or generated truncation wrappers and derived excerpts are omitted with an explicit reason. UTF-8 subprocess decoding preserves split characters within the byte limit. Native MCP tools remain separate. Branch markers survive resume and reload. Fork copies remain historical. Tree navigation creates a new activation; compaction preserves pending sources until settlement. Sources: docs/PI_HOST.md, tests/test_pi_host.py.

Pi requires a fresh user after activation before assistant/tool capture. Historical automatic continuation is omitted because its privacy state is unknown. Shutdown clears pending observations and automatic context. Common ancestry cannot establish episode identity. Sources: pi/extension.ts:92-177, pi_host.py:43-78, docs/PI_HOST.md.

The shared capture boundary claims hashed native identity before privacy transitions. Replays return body-free receipts without rewinding gates. Deleted sources cannot resurrect. Interrupted claims have an unknown outcome and are not replayed. Existing source and queue transactions remain authoritative. Sources: host.py:142-156, store.py:1819-1874.

Native Codex private prompts create their immediate marker before SQLite, then an empty native-identity receipt. Completed replays skip the marker. An interrupted or invalid receipt stays conservative; it cannot establish source capture. Public transitions use shared delivery deduplication. Private prompts create no redacted placeholder source. Sources: hooks.py:302-326,633-662, private_gate.py:50-77, tests/test_hook_privacy_deadline.py.

cards.title: How memory accumulates
items: Each host adapter saves each permitted observation and project memory event in one transaction. A notification speeds up processing. The background service also discovers pending work itself. Sources: store.py:1876-2066, service.py:908-958.

Batch readiness depends on inactivity, age, size, and checkpoints. A Stop event is optional. Each scheduled batch covers one session. A shared session alone does not merge tasks. Source: project_memory.py:299-335,1125-1130.

Before background processing, the brief can show provisional signals from pending events. These include user corrections, requests to remember, decision intent, or saved execution results. Retrieval computes these signals. They remain provisional. Sources: project_memory.py:240-265,1099-1123,1273-1300.

The generator receives a bounded batch and the previous state. It proposes episodes, requirements, decisions, tasks, and links. Each attempt enters the usage ledger before dispatch. A retry gets a separate cost record. Source: episode_processor.py:874-994.

After eligible event batches, discovery can schedule a bounded reconsideration job for split heads with the same positive task identity in original user evidence. It reuses pm_jobs and retained observations. It does not replay a transcript. A completed fingerprint prevents repeated no-op calls for unchanged candidates. Sources: project_memory.py:381-483,1331-1349.

Ordinary event jobs can disclose historical original sources for matching task IDs within their existing input budget. Historical sources do not advance the event queue again. Disclosure reports omitted heads, ancestor chains, and sources. Sources: project_memory.py:336-379,955-961.

Commit records neutral custody identities and offsets for newly consumed user source fragments in the same transaction as queue progress. Reconsideration and historical disclosure do not backfill custody. Source text stays in the existing source store. Sources: project_memory.py:989-997, project_memory_custody.py:12-37.

Storage retries and failure receipts share one contention classifier. Numeric SQLite metadata is authoritative. Without it, only the exact built-in OperationalError messages for a locked database or table map to contention codes. Exception text stays private. Only a failure before the transaction begins can authorize a safe retry; a commit failure never replays the operation. Sources: observation_diagnostics.py:39-84, store.py:994-1055.

cards.title: Who can change state
items: The model proposes changes. ProjectMemory.commit controls database writes. It validates the active lease, source text, revision, deletion generation, and current episode head. Objects, links, custody records, the current head, and queue progress commit in one transaction. Sources: project_memory.py:634-834,888-972.

A job reserves a logical episode only after its continuation evidence passes. Unsupported requests stay standalone with an explicit continuity omission and do not block a supported continuation. Two supported successors of one logical episode, or overlapping continuation and consolidation targets, reject the whole batch. Sources: project_memory.py:729-791.

ProjectMemory.prepare uses the same final assembly as commit, including historical prior_ fields. Optional assessment runs outside the write transaction. Commit rebuilds the records and compares the assessed digest. Preparation grants no lease and bypasses no source or revision guard. Sources: project_memory.py:836-957, episode_processor.py:998-1011.

Unsupported completion or acceptance becomes a proposal. Unsupported links that close or replace records are omitted. These cases require reconciliation. An exact quote proves that the text exists. It does not prove that the field purpose or full conclusion follows from the text. Sources: project_memory.py:689-722,780-800.

Deletion revokes dependent records and episode descendants. It clears a deleted current head and invalidates old jobs. The previous version does not become current automatically. Custody source references cascade on source deletion. Sources: project_memory.py:99-156, project_memory_custody.py:12-18, store.py:5935-6002.

A reconsideration proposal can continue one current head and consolidate other eligible heads. Exact source spans must support explicit continuity and the same task identity. Commit creates a new immutable version and dependency links. Original records stay addressable. Consolidation does not close open claims. Sources: project_memory.py:766-791,925-954,1391-1480.

Discovery inspects at most 100 heads and 64 identity sources totaling 24,000 characters. A job uses at most four heads, eight ancestors per head, 32 retained sources, and 24,000 source characters. Lower caller limits apply. A larger group uses the oldest three heads and newest head. Metadata reports omissions and incomplete history. Source: project_memory.py:381-483.

New heads rebuild earlier goals, reasons, outcomes, and open work in prior_ fields from each field's own disclosed original references. Earlier model prose is not copied. Missing or oversized historical context increments the omission count. Current validity stays unresolved. This does not create or reopen active claims. Source: project_memory.py:836-892.

Native output v12 excludes project membership and object identity from generated values. Code binds omitted worktree scope to the claimed project and object identity to array position. Each claim owns its required outgoing_relations. Trusted code supplies the origin and flattens them into unchanged canonical relations. Empty claims cannot express a native relation. Existing targets and evidence remain required. Explicit canonical foreign values still fail storage validation. Sources: episode_processor.py:45-140,413-463, project_memory.py:693-701.

Storage code assembles episode summary, goal, rationale, outcome, and open_work, plus claim rationale, from each field's own original source sentences. Text carries source-role labels, original offsets, and field_provenance. Field association remains model-selected. Assistant and tool statements retain their original roles. Sources: project_memory.py:792-797,1030-1072.

A current attributed field must fit 6,000 characters and 32 references. Assembled objects and relations must fit 180,000 serialized characters. Oversized current output is rejected atomically. Source sentences cut by a disclosed-body boundary carry partial-context labels. Earlier stored versions are not retroactively verified. Sources: project_memory.py:871-892,1030-1072.

A supported affirmative user command to reopen one confirmed task ID can support continuity. English accepts one short for/to/because explanation. Russian accepts для/чтобы/потому что. The recognizer rejects questions, known negations, conditions, approval-dependent wording, quoted examples, tool reports, and distinct-task wording. Unrecognized wording stays unresolved. Claim transitions use separate checks. Sources: project_memory.py:1342-1514.

A custody row is source bookkeeping, not a separate requirement claim. This does not negate an explicit request inside the original user source. Only eligible whole-source exact-text claims can establish complete representation. Paraphrases, overlap, and partial compound clauses leave custody unresolved. Closure links can project completion. Replacement returns custody to unresolved. Cancellation is not inferred. Session exclusion applies to the source, represented claim, and transition evidence. Source: project_memory_custody.py:40-140.

Event processing uses project-memory-v4. Reconsideration fingerprints use task-consolidation-v4. These policy identifiers do not migrate earlier records or prove deployment. Source: project_memory.py:22-23,314-318,408-453.

Native v11 indexed relations and mixed layouts reject the whole batch. Code neither invents an origin nor silently drops a malformed relation. Native arrays have per-owner bounds; code additionally enforces eight relations across all owners. Canonical injected outputs and storage remain unchanged, without migration or backfill. Structural ownership does not prove target relevance or semantic support. Sources: episode_processor.py:122-140,413-463,905-910.

cards.title: What the agent receives
items: One builder serves explicit briefs, startup context, and part of resume search. The query limits the project, task, version, and retrieval purpose. Retrieval uses current versions by default. Supported current-assessment frames can include prior versions; explicit historical-slice requests can return coverage-only refusal. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101 integration.py:70-132.

Project memory is off by default. Shadow mode processes selected roots and supports explicit reads. Pilot mode adds project state to automatic context. Each worktree requires separate access. Source: config.py:223-246.

At startup, project memory receives up to three fifths of the remaining context budget. Legacy notes fill the remaining space. Saved text carries an untrusted label and unverified freshness. Sources: store.py:5890-5933, hooks.py:856-879.

The brief renders prior_goal, prior_rationale, prior_outcome, and prior_open_work as historical fields. It includes their original source pointers and unresolved-current-validity status. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

The brief renders complete exact quotation groups with source IDs, roles, and original offsets. A group that cannot fit is omitted whole. The renderer reserves bounded room for later obligations, open work, reasons, and source custody before an early record consumes space with secondary outcomes. Oversized reservations do not block a fitting primary group. Omission counts remain visible when space permits. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Natural-language projections prefer open work and reasons before incidental outcomes and summaries. Rationale and environment projections keep separate priorities. Complete emitted intervals can suppress repeated quotations from the same source field and role. Suppressed inferred episode field associations remain counted in field_associations_omitted. Source availability is not complete representation of every inferred field. Oversized groups leave smaller alternatives eligible. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Unresolved custody sources remain render candidates even when candidate material covers their source. Only complete intervals actually emitted from the same source ID, field and role can suppress a redundant fallback. A candidate field that later fails to fit never counts as displayed evidence. Suppression changes display only and never discharges custody. Source rows remain original user text, without a separate requirement claim. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101 project_memory_custody.py:121-140.

Custody filters source identities through the existing entries_fts index before applying the candidate limit. This keeps matching later sources eligible without a body scan or a second search index. Coverage separately reports matched, unmatched, and matched-but-omitted sources. Matching does not infer a user obligation. Sources: project_memory_custody.py:75-146, project_memory.py:233-238.

The local planner recognizes conservative complete English frames for subject-free outcome, evidence-purpose, latest-request relation and assistant-role questions. A current assessment of an earlier assistant claim can include earlier episode versions and execution evidence. Explicit as-of wording keeps its historical scope. Residual topic words retain lexical matching. Exact task IDs, identifiers, versions and environments keep their constraints. Comparison inflections such as compared and comparing select comparative evidence rather than an as-of slice. This selects evidence without judging the claim. Sources: project_memory_query.py:70-182,184-633 project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Query-specific original assistant reports and validated execution records can reach the reader independently of extracted field citations. The source store applies project and query FTS constraints before selecting at most sixteen candidates per role and returning at most two. Privacy, task, version, environment, excluded-session and deletion guards still apply. Assistant reports must fit their complete source within 1,200 characters. Oversized or invalid source records remain omitted with coverage counts. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Original-role records preserve attribution. An assistant report establishes only what the assistant reported. Validated native captures keep the actual command, exit code and complete output in one atomic group. Every direct pointer keeps its own role, field, source ID, offsets and tool-use ID. A checked complete pair can factor repeated completeness metadata into complete_capture_fields=true. Unknown or conflicting item values remain. No lifecycle or completion relation is created. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:620-676,1001-1167, project_memory_source_transport.py:85-161.

A complete custody source of at most 600 characters can receive a compact whole-group reservation. The total reserve uses at most one third of the available brief, capped at 2,000 characters. For sources overlapping material, this reserve protects reason evidence. Quotations are never shortened to create that fallback. Larger groups fit whole or remain omitted. The budget does not guarantee every relevant source appears. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Bounded first-role protection can retain a whole native execution before user originals. Further eligible captures compete after complete selected user transport. An unrecognized frame protects one execution within min(1800,budget//3) and one small report within min(900,budget//6). Explicit evidence requests can use expanded protection. The captured command, exit and full output remain indivisible. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:1001-1167.

At least two eligible unresolved user-source intervals can share a neutral original-source bundle. Each chosen interval stays whole with source ID, role, offsets and capture sequence. Selection tries newest intervals first, then displays selected intervals in capture order. A bundle selects at most eight intervals of at most 600 characters each. Its XML uses at most 3,200 characters and must fit after reserved execution and current-head evidence. Missing intervals receive explicit omission counts. Partial consumed sources keep their interval status. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Hard task, identifier, version, environment, project, privacy, session and deletion guards still apply to original user sources. Soft relevance can keep a source already cited by eligible material only after hard query matching passes. Bundle presence creates no requirement, completion, continuity or contradiction relation, and extends no retention. Matching worktree and capture-order qualifiers move to the XML root only when opening and closing tags fit; otherwise record qualifiers remain subject to fit-or-omit. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Complete observed tool fields keep a bounded reservation when native execution shape is unavailable. A compact omitted latest-head identity is added after material rendering when it fits. It can trim lower-priority coverage counters but never a fitting quotation. Version and uncertainty metadata do not imply that omitted fields were shown. Default total budget remains 6,000 characters. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

The shared planner separates caller-selected project scope names from content in the brief builder and Store.context. The owner remains implicit. At most sixteen additional absolute canonical paths require enabled project memory. Unique exact structured basenames can repeat selected scope metadata in natural requests; ordinary alphabetic names require explicit scope syntax. Quoted, code-like, ambiguous, unknown and unselected names retain their content constraints. Normalization discovers no project and expands no read owner. The MCP state read accepts selected_project_scopes. ProjectMemory.snapshot remains literal. Sources: project_memory_query.py:70-182,474-601, store.py:5698-5707, mcp.py:810-822.

A leading selected-scope clause with a comma can precede a recognized natural request even when it ends with a period. Code-only bodies and unknown, ambiguous or quoted scope names retain literal behavior. Protected task, version, environment, command and artifact positions remain exact. A bare conjunction does not promote an unprotected descriptive hyphen compound to an identifier. The original query remains; only soft matching splits that compound into words. Scope-list syntax preserves existing hard coordinated names. These bounded grammar rules infer no source meaning or current truth. Sources: project_memory_query.py:92-182,474-601.

Complete requirement-state clauses describe answer fields without requiring words such as cancelled or retained in each source. Generic project-state selection requires no residual topic or exact subject; remaining topics remain content constraints. This selects evidence without inferring cancellation, replacement or current validity. Declared environment scope remains a hard boundary. User words do not establish an execution environment. Unscoped user quotes keep unknown scope and user attribution. Raw environment checks apply to tool and assistant evidence; inferred claims are checked against their own execution references. Environment projections reject complete groups containing incompatible execution and never restore all-filtered fields. Sources: project_memory_query.py:70-182,184-633 project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Neutral custody can use declared environment metadata only from a current whole-source exact user claim. Binding requires the same source ID, body field, user role, full body span and exact text, with all references on that original user source. Partial, mixed, historical, episode, report and retired associations cannot bind it. Owner, worktree, privacy, session and deletion guards apply. The metadata is an environment guard only; it assigns no quote scope, content anchor or custody fate. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Custody scope association is limited to sixty-four claim candidates per source. Overflow omits the source and reports custody_scope_binding_lookups_omitted. Conflicting exact declarations report custody_scope_conflicts: environment-scoped reads omit the source, while unscoped reads can keep its quote with conflicting_declared_environment_scopes uncertainty. No conflict becomes proof of unrestricted applicability. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Scope filtering preserves normative user text without promoting it to observed execution. Canonical declared scope is enforced, and actual assistant or tool quotations still cannot conceal an opposite execution environment. Inferred claims keep the scope of their own execution references. Mixed environment projections reject whole incompatible groups and provide no fallback to filtered original fields. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Original user sources share a bundle only when their record metadata match, including lane, kind, role, disposition, requirement-claim flag, meaning and uncertainty. Different markers remain in separate containers, including single-source groups. A conflict warning is neither discarded nor applied to an unrelated source. Capture-order and whole-group budget rules remain unchanged. Source: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Complete complementary episode-source intervals retain their own source ID, field, role and qualifiers. Only consistent adjacent or overlapping intervals join, within the 600-character bound. Custody and native capture IDs stay separate in this complementary pool. Original excerpts carry field_association=not_assessed and establish no new execution validity or field judgment. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:811-874,893-998,1505-1610.

Exact quoted-value duplication can omit derived prose only when same-source references reconstruct the value in their original contiguous order. Pointers, field metadata, roles and state/scope qualifiers remain. Paraphrases keep separate prose. Evidence questions can also reserve one sixth of the brief, capped at 900 characters, for small original assistant reports. More complete evidence can displace incidental quotations. These rules do not establish compression or quality acceptance. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Complete authorized, unfinished and continuation-requirement frames retain all residual topic terms. Evidence facets change allocation, not eligibility. Ordinary source words can use bounded plural-prefix matching; identifiers and versions remain exact. Bare original is not a historical request; explicit as-of and past-original questions keep history behavior. Source: project_memory_query.py:70-182,184-633; project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

The planner exposes answer_subject, answer_facets and source_order. Grammatical requirement, current-revision, reason and execution-assessment instructions do not replace residual topical matching. Positive or negative question wording does not filter the answer polarity. Exact owner, task, identifier, version, environment, session, privacy and deletion guards remain. Source: project_memory_query.py:70-182,184-633.

The early user-source plan uses already admitted evidence. Inferred prior_ source IDs stay outside inferred user groups, but cannot suppress an independently qualified complete original in source custody. Its disposition and unresolved applicability remain explicit. Complete user intervals join within 1,200 characters. Per-source capture sequence takes precedence over episode ranges; the metadata lookup remains bounded to sixty-four selected source IDs. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:811-874,893-998,2070-2101.

Recognized first/initial/earliest and last/latest operation queries order the existing scoped sixteen-candidate window before returning two records per role. Execution groups can be promoted before other records. Capture order is local ingestion order, not event time or proof of operation identity. Native atomic command/exit/full-output and all hard source guards remain. Sources: project_memory_query.py:70-182,184-633, project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Ordinary nonhistorical natural queries outside continuation and ordinal lookup can read a finite original-context pool even without soft lexical overlap. recent_context=True returns whole retained user originals of at most 600 characters before the newest-sixteen cap, including stored/completed dispositions without asserting current applicability. Default and recent_unresolved reads remain available. Guard metadata arrives with exact text; no raw-user FTS lane or extra Store.get body fetch is added. Sources: project_memory_custody.py:75-146, project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Unknown soft topics no longer imply empty transport. Neutral originals pass exact project, task-ID, literal, version, environment, session, privacy, deletion and history guards independently. Their query relationship stays unresolved; they establish no task association, active requirement or current truth. Previously represented user observations keep their disposition and current_applicability_unresolved uncertainty. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

Whole neutral user originals compete within min(1800,budget//3) and capacity after protecting selected original executions/reports. Exact complete group and omission-marker costs replace the three-source cutoff; acquisition windows remain bounded. Latest capture is tried first, then earliest. Identical qualifiers alone can share a container; role, meaning, uncertainty and unresolved query relationship remain explicit. The finite neutral assistant/tool window has sixteen candidates per role, two returns per role and a 1,200-character body bound. Whole tool command/exit/output remains atomic. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

A quote_ref resolves exact original provenance through a source-only ID. The root declares quote_refs=provenance_only. Reference bounds can select an exact original subinterval. Scope, history, custody, workflow, uncertainty and query relationship stay local to each association. Unknown pointer qualifiers and adjacent-statement context_basis remain explicit. A reference never inherits a target container's association qualifiers. Different roles, fields, events and tool-use identities do not become aliases. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:691-713,1505-1610, project_memory_source_transport.py:14-84.

Checked original environment and version qualifiers survive record construction and rendering even for unscoped questions. Code carries scoped_original into the custody record, never the query scope or temporary environment guard. Known, unknown and differing original scopes remain separate without inferring current applicability. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:31-152,376-502,620-1610,1613-2101.

One primary plan allocates already admitted complete material originals before optional neutral context. Per-source capture sequence wins over episode ranges. Exact original quotation transport is shared while distinct association qualifiers remain separate. Neutral originals use the bounded candidate windows and min(1800,budget//3), with actual marker-aware prices. Candidate-limit metadata does not promise all sources will fit. Primary admission remains conservative and does not promise maximal packing; owner quotas do not move between projects. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:893-998,1001-1492.

After primary selection, checked XML compaction can fund whole complementary source groups without evicting selected quotations or associations. A complete omitted typed claim association may refill only when its exact source spans are already displayed and its reference node fits the final wire. It keeps its own workflow, scope, field purpose and uncertainty; references share only provenance. Existing source IDs cannot collide across source, role, field, interval or tool identity. Only exact root-shared worktree/capture qualifiers factor at the root. Other inferred associations can remain omitted. Both render paths use this step; mandatory declaration cost and the single primary retry remain explicit. Reads call no model and change no stored state. Visibility replay is not quality acceptance. Sources: project_memory_retrieval.py:1495-1610,2092-2101, project_memory_source_transport.py:85-161.

Complete current request-fate and task-reference questions can remove incidental earlier/later historical interpretation. A relation question selects continuity projection without asserting continuation or task identity. Explicit as-of, genuine history, date, version and all hard source guards remain. Source visibility does not establish supported answers or current truth. Source: project_memory_query.py:184-275,498-633.

Natural questions can use an unquoted alphabetic hyphen compound as a modifier before an ordinary word. Every occurrence must have that form. Function words, calls, camel case and explicit literal or unknown project labels preserve identity constraints. Matching input alone splits soft compounds; source bytes and intervals stay exact. This bounded grammar does not prove meaning or task association. Sources: project_memory_query.py:184-205,498-633.

cards.title: Boundaries and optional features
items: Sources, queues, and derived records stay local. The selected runtime sends prepared evidence to its configured model provider. Codex retains its existing isolation. Pi restricts model tools and extension discovery without claiming OS isolation; openai-codex review loads only the explicit bundled schema helper. Native auth/model configuration and the installed executable remain trusted. Sources: processor.py:1005-1220,1753-1791, pi_runtime.py:167-181,368-400,453-491.

The note processor and project memory use the same execution contract. Issue #8 activates Pi for observations and summaries as well as project memory. Their queues and atomic commits remain independent, and profile changes do not replay successful sources. Sources: processor.py:647-716, episode_processor.py:943-1026, execution.py:206-211.

Local E5 supplements legacy search. Jev can separately assess generator output or rank legacy context. Configuration controls these external calls. The local brief works without them. Sources: semantic.py:37-47,534-610, store.py:5860-5868, episode_processor.py:998-1005.

When enabled, the existing Jev quality gate checks final assembled fields, including prior_ fields, against their own exact source spans. It also checks original proposed_value interpretations when assembly changed the model wording. Exact copying cannot hide an unsupported proposal. Full context can qualify but cannot replace cited support. The gate checks support and overclaim, not external truth. The measured field-purpose workflow remains experimental, without a production blocker. Sources: episode_processor.py:724-795,777-802,914-927, jev_quality.py:1-7.

The quality gate checks payload bounds for all fields before dispatch. Batches share a 20-second evaluation budget. More fields can require more calls or exceed payload limits. A rejected or uncertain result prevents the batch commit. This optional model check does not prove field relevance, current validity, or overall correctness. Sources: episode_processor.py:854-871,914-960, jev_quality.py:16-23.

cards.title: Maintenance and limits
items: When capture, processing, storage, retrieval, or provider boundaries change, review the diagram and source links. Update candidate.json and rebuild the HTML with Archify. AGENTS.md requires this work in the same task.

maintain.py check compares source files and hashes with the snapshot. It also compares the specification and HTML with their saved hashes. Code changes require a review of the architecture descriptions. Matching hashes alone do not prove that the diagram is complete.

Memory covers saved observations. It does not contain the complete transcript. An empty queue does not prove that external project information is current. Bounded reconsideration does not repair every historical split or prove answer quality. Prompt changes do not automatically repair old records. Source: docs/PROJECT_MEMORY.md, Understand evidence and coverage.

The October 21 semantic development probe records its fixed policy, labels, failed first attempt, supervised retry, probabilities, and usage under docs/evidence/project-memory-quality-2026-10-21/field-*. The narrow check reduced false acceptance but left useful fields uncertain. It was not enabled as a blocking check. This disclosed development set is not an independent acceptance benchmark. Source hashes and rendered output do not establish semantic quality or production deployment.

cards.title: Pi native MCP tools
items: Pi 1.4.0 connects to the existing Python MCP server. One configured server owns tool discovery and calls. The lifecycle extension captures completed events without registering duplicate tools. Explicit reads need no background runtime. Sources: docs/pi-mcp.example.json:1-17, docs/PI_MCP.md:1-25.

The example hides mutation capabilities until the user enables them. Project arguments retain the existing Store partition; this is not a current-directory sandbox. Deterministic installed-Pi RPC tests cover real native MCP and a temporary Store, not live-provider quality or Pi background execution. Sources: docs/PI_MCP.md:15-25, tests/test_pi_mcp.py:185-305.

Shared raw-tool sanitization redacts credential-named structured fields before serialization, including object and array values. Readback sanitizes legacy rows and regenerates excerpts without mutating stored bytes, source IDs, or historical hashes; view metadata discloses changes. Malformed payloads and all truncation-wrapper fragments plus derived excerpts are omitted with bounded reasons, because incomplete JSON cannot prove nested-secret removal. Ordinary nonsecret values keep their types. This applies to Codex and Pi source reads. Sources: codex_mem/privacy.py:40-53, codex_mem/tool_io.py:425-437,562-572,1055-1071, tests/test_mcp.py:166-274.
